svg.title: Indeed the free derivative map is nonzero: its divergence target contains a nonzero coordinate and is attained; if every observer vanished on every first derivative, the separating observers would make that target zero, a contradiction. Choose an observer with a nonzero derivative value y. Its free translation-flux Ward identity has value y. The corresponding physical shell-flux test of R, with positions, cutoffand fields scaled together and with the single factor ri prescribed by the derivative, tends to y. If R = 0, every such test would be zero, contradicting y ̸= 0. Since the kernel is one-dimensional, eTi = viR for real vi eventually. The shell-flux test of R tends to y, while its test on eTi also tends to y, by (TR43) and the tested derivative comparison.
